title: 200+ Shells Hit This Wooden Tower in 1926 — Still Standing | China Travel Expert
description:
In 1926, during the warlord war between Feng Yuxiang and Yan Xishan, the Yingxian Wooden Pagoda in Shanxi took more than 200 artillery shells — and never fell. It's the Sakyamuni Pagoda of Fogong Temple, built in 1056: about 67 m of timber, raised with interlocking dougong brackets and mortise-and-tenon joints, not a single nail.

Why didn't it topple? The frame is built to move. Two rings of columns form a tube inside a tube; what looks like 5 storeys actually hides 9 internal levels whose bracket sets stiffen each ring. When shells — or earthquakes — hit, the joints slip a little and burn off the energy, so the whole tower sways and twists instead of snapping. It's ridden out centuries of quakes the same way.

★ Expert Tip: look closely at the upper storeys — columns on the 3rd and 5th floors still lean from the 1926 (and 1948) shelling, which is why conservation now limits how far up visitors can go.

1926年冯阎大战，应县木塔中弹二百余发而不倒——以柔克刚，榫卯斗拱让它摇而不断。
